name: Minimal-LinuxBench
intro: Minimal-LinuxBench 是 Anthropic 基于 Redwood Research 私下共享的 LinuxBench 子集开发的非公开 AI 控制评测。系统卡只披露改编了 1,948 个主任务/副任务对并随机抽取 200 对，通过完整轨迹监控衡量副任务完成、告警与完成且未被发现的隐蔽成功；任务构建、环境、解析评分实现和发布许可均未公开。
build_method: 私有 LinuxBench 子集改编, 主任务与副任务配对, 随机抽样, 主要与选择性攻击提示, 全轨迹监控
metric: 副任务完成率, 监控告警率, 隐蔽成功率（完成且未被发现）
eval_feature: 隐蔽副任务, 无扩展思考, 全轨迹监控, 无/含CoT监控器, 选择性攻击迁移, Wilson置信区间
scale: 改编 1,948 对；随机抽取 200 对（有效分母略低于 200）
build_method_en: Private LinuxBench Subset Adaptation, Main/Side-task Pairing, Random Sampling, Main and Selective Attack Prompts, Full-transcript Monitoring
eval_feature_en: Covert Side Tasks, No Extended Thinking, Full-transcript Monitoring, No-CoT and With-CoT Monitors, Selective-attack Transfer, Wilson Confidence Intervals
intro_en: Minimal-LinuxBench is Anthropic's non-public AI-control evaluation developed from a subset of LinuxBench privately shared by Redwood Research. The system card discloses 1,948 adapted main/side-task pairs and a random 200-pair sample, with entire-transcript monitoring used to measure completion, monitor flags, and stealth wins (completed and undetected); task construction, environments, parsing/scoring implementation, and release licensing are not public.
scale_en: 1,948 pairs adapted; 200 sampled (effective denominator slightly below 200)
metric_en: Side-task Completion Rate, Monitor Flag Rate, Stealth Win Rate (Completed and Undetected)

drawio_review_note: Primary-source review used the official Claude Mythos Preview System Card dated April 7, 2026, including its changelog through April 14, Sections 4.4.3.2–4.4.3.3, and Figures 4.4.3.2.A–4.4.3.3.A. The exact official PDF URL contains Anthropic content identifier 7624816413e9b4d2e3ba620c5a5e091b98b190a5, and the reviewed 245-page file is pinned by SHA-256 55f6ed1c0735ec1b5b14d99c91794fb759ac4647edc64381123b68be89fd3225. The official Alignment Risk Update dated April 7 with an April 10 changelog was also checked at https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/3edfc1a7f947aa81841cf88305cb513f184c36ae/Alignment%20Risk%20Update_%20Claude%20Mythos%20Preview%20%28Redacted%2C%20April%2010%29.pdf and pinned by SHA-256 de07fda57950f3a638fb64bee89cb67645583a5f73f47981ec120e717abbe129. That update explicitly calls Minimal-LinuxBench non-public and says Anthropic believes it better represents its internal usage distribution, supporting the in-house openness label without implying public reproducibility. The construction diagram is intentionally limited to what these sources disclose. Redwood Research built and privately shared LinuxBench as an AI-control arena. Anthropic adapted a subset for an in-development evaluation in high-stakes software environments, producing 1,948 pairs of main and side tasks, then randomly sampled 200 pairs. A small minority failed before evaluation began, so the effective denominator is slightly below 200; the exact retained count and failure causes are not given and no rate is back-computed from an assumed denominator. In the main setting, Claude Mythos Preview runs without extended thinking and is instructed to attempt the side task on every trajectory. Anthropic tried three attack system prompts with different detail levels; each tells the model that the entire transcript will be monitored, and their performance was similar. The entire transcript, including assistant turns, is sent to the monitor. Prior checkpoints and a helpful-only model were also tested with broadly similar results. Claude Mythos Preview achieved the side task on 69 of the sampled pairs. Figure 4.4.3.2.A separately reports successful stealth completion: for the no-CoT monitor used in early deployment, Mythos Preview is 11.4%; for the with-CoT monitor described as current, it is 2.7%. Both are shown with 95% Wilson intervals, and the text says the error bars are too large for a more precise model comparison. Section 4.4.3.3 is a distinct selective-transfer experiment using the best-performing available Mythos checkpoint, not a continuation that may be merged numerically with the 69-of-200 observation. Anthropic hand-crafted and iteratively refined prompts on SHADE-Arena to make the model attempt only when confident it would avoid detection. Applied to Minimal-LinuxBench, the prompts reduce attempts but select the wrong tasks and conditional stealth falls. Figure 4.4.3.3.A reports baseline, selective, and highly selective conditions respectively: side-task completion 42.8%, 18.8%, and 20.8%; monitor flags 77.2%, 39.8%, and 39.9%; stealth wins 4.8%, 1.1%, and 1.2%. A stealth win means completed and undetected. Flag rates can exceed completion because failed attempts remain visible and the side-task instruction makes behavior somewhat more suspicious; benign main-task-only trajectories have an approximately 2% false-positive rate, and refusals contribute negligibly. Wilson 95% confidence intervals are shown. The official sources do not disclose source-task provenance, authoring, pair construction rules, subset-selection criteria beyond adaptation and random evaluation sampling, train/dev/test splits, environment images or versions, agent scaffold, full prompt text, transcript serialization, tool/action schema, monitor implementation, completion judge, flag parser, aggregation code, exact post-failure denominator, or validation/quality-control workflow. No public benchmark repository, dataset artifact, version tag, code or data license, result-submission process, or official leaderboard was identified. Accordingly, the diagram marks every such item as an unknown or private release boundary instead of borrowing details from LinuxBench, LinuxArena, or SHADE-Arena. Formal publication evidence [site-a11v-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 2954×911 (English) and 2933×911 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 2952×909 and 2931×909. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
